title: What is social engineering? (IBM Security explainer)
notes: Read live via curl on 2026-08-21; reputable vendor explainer used as a secondary source. Facts synthesized; no wording reproduced.

title: Database normalization
notes: Tier D reputable secondary. Read live via curl 2026-08-21. Supports: normalization as structuring a relational database according to normal forms to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity; the idea first proposed by Edgar F. Codd as part of his relational model (1NF defined by Codd in 1970, 2NF and 3NF in 1971); the three anomalies (insertion, update, deletion) with the update-anomaly example of one employee shown with different addresses on different records; the informal statement that a relation is described as normalized if it meets third normal form, with most 3NF relations free of the three anomalies; the existence of higher forms (BCNF, 4NF, 5NF, 6NF). Used for attribution, the anomalies framing, and the 3NF-as-common-target statement. Facts synthesized into original prose; no wording reproduced.

title: Wikipedia: Database transaction
notes: Tier C supplementary reference. Read live 2026-08-21. title: Misleading graph
notes: Read live 2026-08-21. Documents the named mechanisms of misleading charts: truncated graphs whose y-axis does not start at 0 can create the impression of important change where there is little; graphs with omitted data remove information from which to base a conclusion; a superfluous third dimension confuses readers because perspective makes equal values look different and three-dimensional scaling cubes the effect; pictograms scaled uniformly are misread by area, making differences appear squared; log scales used without clear labeling mislead; changing the y-axis maximum changes apparent growth. Also notes Darrell Huff's 1954 book 'How to Lie with Statistics' as an early popular treatment of misleading graphs and describes the lie factor concept. Tier D reference used for the misleading-chart taxonomy; facts synthesized into original examples.
